about: Every labelling rule in force (golden/rules.md), with the sentences in the readers' guide that carry it. golden/rules.test.js fails when a sentence listed here is no longer in the guide, so a rule cannot be dropped from the prompt by accident. To change a rule's wording on purpose, change the guide and the sentence here in the same commit.

rules.name: Label the article, not what Anton cares about
guide_must_say: Answer what the article is, not what a reader would want.

rules.name: Only the saved text counts
guide_must_say: reading the whole saved text
is not the article's content
do his own words appear in the saved text

rules.name: Only what is new
guide_must_say: All nine answers describe the article's one main claim.
it does not set the fact, and it does not turn a yes/no question to yes

rules.name: No fact means nothing else either
guide_must_say: When the fact is no_fact, firmness is none and the three news questions (result, next fight, health) are no.

rules.name: A fact stated inside the main claim belongs to it
guide_must_say: a fact stated inside the main claim belongs to it

rules.name: The three news questions: the main fact or a second fact, never a mention
guide_must_say: as the main fact, or as a second fact stated beside it
They never mean "is it mentioned"

rules.name: New, not long
guide_must_say: judge what is new about him, not how long his part is

rules.name: Talking about someone else
guide_must_say: when nothing in the article comes back to him

rules.name: A callout is the other fighter's story
guide_must_say: is that fighter's story, never main_subject
a fighter only rumoured or calling him out does not count

rules.name: A two-fighter preview is one of several
guide_must_say: a preview or feature on a fight of his covering both fighters

rules.name: Booked or fought
guide_must_say: Booked or fought only
does not make him an opponent

rules.name: Another fighter's camp is "other fighter's side"
guide_must_say: or that fighter's coach, manager or team

rules.name: A fighter is a fighter, active or retired
guide_must_say: A fighter is a fighter, active or retired

rules.name: An act needs a plain statement about him
guide_must_say: An act needs a plain statement about him
gives_news_of_him is never the act when question 4 is no_fact

rules.name: A callout is not only a literal callout
guide_must_say: Not only a literal callout
Mock advice is calls_him_out

rules.name: "Speaks of himself" is only for the watched fighter
guide_must_say: speaks_of_himself is only possible with source himself

rules.name: Next fight means a specific fight exists or changes
guide_must_say: news that a specific fight of his exists or has changed
It counts when he himself says he has a fight

rules.name: A rumour needs a who, a when or a where
guide_must_say: A rumour counts only when the article gives it substance: who said it, or a date or event

rules.name: A wish is no fact, whoever makes it
guide_must_say: Wishes, demands, callouts, picks and guesses at his timing are all no_fact, whoever makes them

rules.name: Status update, after the specific kinds
guide_must_say: Pick the specific value first
news of where he stands as a fighter

rules.name: Health wins over a return date
guide_must_say: however briefly, the fact is health

rules.name: Health follows who states it
guide_must_say: states his condition as a statement of its own

rules.name: A post or letter takes the label of what it says
guide_must_say: takes the value of what it says

rules.name: Result only for an account of the fight itself
guide_must_say: Yes only for an account of the fight itself
An account of the fight itself; a statement, interview or callout after it takes the value of what is said

rules.name: An interview is a place, not a fact
guide_must_say: is a place where things are said, not a fact

rules.name: His own unsigned fight is "reported"
guide_must_say: when he says he has a fight but it is not signed or announced, that is reported

rules.name: He speaks only when his words are there
guide_must_say: Also no when a post or statement of his is only described and not quoted (#44), or when the only words of his are a few recalled from an earlier occasion as background (#823).
